title: Error path sets columns to [] without updating prevColumnFingerprint, can wedge state empty against a later equal-schema cache
description: The fetch .catch handler does `if (!cachedColumnsRef.current) setDataInputColumns([])` but never updates `prevColumnFingerprint.current`. Every OTHER place that calls setDataInputColumns first writes the new fingerprint into prevColumnFingerprint (lines 102, 111, 118, 127, 132, 156). After a no-cache error with a NON-empty `fallbackColumns`, state becomes [] while prevColumnFingerprint still holds fp(fallback). If the store cache is later populated externally with columns whose fingerprint equals that stale prev (e.g. the same schema as the fallback), the sync effect (lines 100-105) compares fp(cache) === prev and SKIPS the update, leaving the hook permanently returning [] even though valid cached columns now exist. The invariant 'prevColumnFingerprint mirrors the currently displayed columns' is silently broken only on this branch.
evidence: Line 166 `if (!cachedColumnsRef.current) setDataInputColumns([])` with no accompanying `prevColumnFingerprint.current = columnFingerprint([])` (which would be the EMPTY_COLUMNS_FINGERPRINT "0:"). Contrast every successful update which pairs the setState with a prev write (e.g. lines 155-157). Reachability: requires `enabled` true with a non-empty `fallbackColumns` (so initial prev = fp(fallback), not "0:"), then a rejected fetch with no cache, then an external cache populate matching the fallback schema. The current sole caller (OptimiserConfig.tsx:277-280) only enables the hook when `fallbackDataInputColumns` is empty, so it avoids the trigger today, but the hook is a reusable public API and the missing fingerprint write is a genuine state-sync defect.
